title: Tenant isolation: burst reservoirs and noisy-neighbor circuit-breaker
creator: Maya Chen
description: We need a tenant-level isolation mechanism that guarantees committed throughput while allowing short bursts. This ticket designs and implements a two-layer protection model: (1) per-tenant burst reservoirs (token-bucket style) to provide short-term throughput elasticity, and (2) a noisy-neighbor circuit-breaker that detects sustained degradation in latency/throughput and triggers graduated mitigation (soft evictions, traffic shaping, fallback routing). The goal is to reduce cross-tenant interference on dedicated GPU pools without hard manual slicing, preserving utilization and predictable SLAs for committed customers.
acceptance_criteria: Committed throughput is met for at least 95% of minutes for tenants with reserved capacity
Burst reservoirs allow 2x baseline throughput for up to 30 seconds without impacting other tenants' SLOs
Circuit-breaker engages when tail latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive minutes and reduces downstream impact by 50% within 60 seconds
All changes are behind a feature flag and can be rolled back per pool
Automated integration tests and chaos tests exist and run in CI for the new controls
technical_design: Introduce per-tenant token-bucket reservoir stored in Redis with lease semantics for multi-replica leaders
Augment scheduler with a tenant-score function combining reserved tokens, recent usage, and estimated queue length
Implement circuit-breaker evaluating moving-window metrics (p99 latency, queue depth, GPU utilization) with hysteresis and backoff
Soft-eviction performs graceful request draining and KPI-weighted demotion to lower-priority lanes
Provide emergency fallback routing to lower-cost model variants and region-level spillovers
Expose control knobs in the console: reservoir size, refill rate, circuit-breaker thresholds, and escalation policy
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable in one Dedicated pool with non-critical tenants, monitor SLOs and false positives for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (expanded): Open to tenants with reserved capacity flags, adjust thresholds based on telemetry for 1 week
Phase 3: Default enablement for new dedicated pools; opt-in for legacy pools for 4 weeks
Fallback: feature-flag rollback automatically reapplies previous scheduling behavior
risks: Incorrect reservoir sizing can starve background batch workloads
Circuit-breaker false positives could throttle legitimate traffic leading to customer impact
Redis lease loss at scale could create transient double-counting of tokens
Interplay with autoscaler needs coordination to avoid cascading scale-ups during circuit-breaker events
mitigation: Start with conservative default reservoir and expose immediate tuning in Console
Add a 'snooze' mode to temporarily disable circuit-breaker for a tenant
Use Raft-backed leader election for token grants in each pool; fall back to local in-memory estimates with limits
Coordination: add supervisor hook so autoscaler ignores short circuit-breaker events when making scale decisions
testing_plan: Unit tests for token-bucket and lease semantics
E2E on staging with synthetic noisy tenants and ramped bursts
Chaos test: inject tenant that consumes infinite tokens and verify circuit-breaker response
Load test: validate scheduler correctness under 500 concurrent tenants
updates: 2026-01-30: Spike completed. Prototype token-bucket in runtime repo and microbenchmark shows <3% overhead on scheduling path.
2026-02-10: Design review with Reliability and PMs. Agreed on moving-window p99 and 3-minute trigger. PM asked for backstop SLA reporting.
2026-02-24: Implemented Redis lease prototype and a local fallback; observed rare lease contention at 2k tenants in lab.
2026-03-05: Canary rollout started in 'eu-west-1-dedicated-2' with 5 low-risk tenants; initial telemetry stable.
2026-03-12: Circuit-breaker threshold adjusted after false positive; added 'snooze' toggle and updated playbook.
creator_notes: Prior art: similar approach used in service-mesh rate-limiters combined with eviction policies. Keep config surface minimal for GA.
